analysis: In congenital heart disease, the presence or absence of pulmonary plethora (increased blood flow to the lungs) helps narrow down the diagnosis. Pulmonary plethora is typically seen in conditions with left-to-right shunts or increased pulmonary blood flow. In this case, the absence of pulmonary plethora suggests a condition with reduced pulmonary blood flow. Tricuspid atresia is a condition where there is an obstruction to blood flow from the right atrium to the right ventricle, leading to reduced pulmonary blood flow and thus no pulmonary plethora. Other options like ventricular communication and persistent truncus arteriosus are associated with increased pulmonary blood flow, and ductus arteriosus is not typically associated with congenital heart disease without pulmonary plethora.
